two_identity_paths: A tokenized <Phrase> key is a MARKER STRING, so it encodes nesting and is sensitive to any tree difference. A content block's custom_id is a flat ORDERED TOKEN ARRAY, so it survives a tree difference that preserves document order. Measured consequence: foster parenting splits the phrase key ONLY, while a raw-text body carrying markup splits BOTH - and the block half is an ARITY change, which per CID-1 re-keys every block containing one. The raw-text family is therefore the more damaging of the two, which is the opposite of this file's first reading.
provenance: libxml2 columns are MEASURED in this repo. JS-family PHRASE keys (the encoded strings) are MEASURED: langsys-js-server @ 8105faa, real Chromium 153 against parse5, 9/9, and independently re-run by the Reviewer against the JS Server's own encodePhrase(). JS-family TOKEN ARRAYS are NOT measured - ALL of them, raw-text rows as well as foster rows, were DERIVED by the TS lane from a hand-modelled tree. An earlier revision of this note caveated only the foster rows, which understated it. The raw-text JS arrays match the fleet's parse5/Chromium behaviour but the TS lane could not have confirmed them: its test DOM (happy-dom) builds a raw-text body the LIBXML2 way, tokens ['a','b','Keep'], block id d55c2b5c806bde213b0637da096c6b36 - byte-identical to this repo's measurement - so their harness agrees with libxml2 there for the wrong reason. The raw-text arity split is real on the parse5 side; only the evidence for its JS half is a derivation, and it should be confirmed by whoever holds parse5 before anyone relies on the token arrays as measured values.
block_id_category: UI. Every *_block_id in this file is HtmlParser::generateCustomId('UI', tokens). The category is PART OF THE HASH, so the ids are not reproducible without it - under the SDK's default '__uncategorized__' the same tokens give different values (e.g. foster-stray-element becomes b67f0bc9259c1341bcca9555db386076). Stated because an id a reader cannot recompute from this file is not evidence.
